recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. Do not make base ValueSet.name or ValueSet.description mandatory again, and do not restore the old core ShareableValueSet profile for this DSTU1 issue; future profile changes should be made in CRMI or through a new tracker that explicitly reverses the later migration decisions.
issue_request: FHIR-3262 was Published/Persuasive for DSTU1 and asked to relax ValueSet.name and ValueSet.description from mandatory base elements to optional metadata because they are good-practice fields, not universally required fields. The 2014 decision also called for usage guidance and noted that a shareable ValueSet definition could enforce good practices for shared value sets.
initial_application: Git-svn commit 4d8eb62cdb50b006a834b9807e19f4e73b59ee51, matching Jira comment svn r2927, changed the then-current source/valueset/valueset-spreadsheet.xml cardinalities for ValueSet.name and ValueSet.description from 1..1 to 0..1 and added comments saying names/descriptions should normally be provided except for contained or context-local value sets.
additional_context: The current source has been refactored into source/valueset/structuredefinition-ValueSet.xml and preserves the optional base cardinalities. Later issues FHIR-29943 and FHIR-31395 changed the separate ShareableValueSet/profile-family behavior, and FHIR-37959 later removed the terminology Shareable/Publishable/Computable/Executable profiles from core for CRMI maintenance. Current fhir.ini has no active ValueSet profile entry and the ValueSet core IG definition has no StructureDefinition references.
reconciliation: No source edit was made. The active ValueSet resource definition already satisfies the seed issue: ValueSet.name and ValueSet.description both have min=0, and both carry SHOULD-level guidance about when the metadata should be present. Reintroducing or editing the old ShareableValueSet profile would conflict with later profile-migration decisions and is outside the current core build scope.
